outputs: translated sentences, generated summaries, language model predictions
The paper evaluates generated outputs in machine translation and abstractive summarization, where models produce translated and summarized text.

changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate model names and generalized dataset names. Consolidated outputs to be more concise. Kept only the main NLG evaluation tasks explicitly evaluated.
Normalized all ROUGE variants to base ROUGE metric. Simplified 'perplexity' to 'Perplexity'. Added base ROUGE form that was missing.
No LLM-as-judge evaluation was conducted in this paper. The paper focuses on architectural improvements to transformers, not LLM evaluation methods.
The paper does not conduct any human evaluations. All evaluations are automated using BLEU, ROUGE, and perplexity metrics.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on improving Multi-Head Attention mechanisms in transformers through grouping and pruning strategies. It evaluates these architectural improvements on standard NLG tasks (MT, summarization, LM) using established automatic metrics. No human or LLM-based evaluation is conducted. The extraction was generally accurate, but needed normalization of metric names and removal of duplicate entries.
